objectives.title: Identity and access management
objectives.statement: Manage the identities and access of agents and of the people who use or operate them, from one place, with access granted for a purpose and taken away when the purpose ends.
objectives.risk: Unauthorized access by an agent or a person
tiers: Sandbox access uses sandbox identities.
Agent and operator access is granted through the identity system and reviewed each year.
Access is reviewed each quarter, and operator access to Tier 3 agents needs a second factor.
Access to Tier 4 agents is granted for a limited time on request, and every use is recorded.
objectives.evidence: The access register and the completed access reviews.

objectives.title: A network fence
objectives.statement: Let each agent reach only the systems named in its declaration, so that a compromised agent cannot move sideways.
objectives.risk: A compromised agent reaching other systems
objectives.metric: Share of agents whose reach is limited to their declared systems
tiers: The sandbox cannot reach production networks.
Each agent's outbound reach is limited to approved destinations.
Reach is limited to the systems in the agent's signed declaration, and attempts to go elsewhere are alerted.
The fence is tested by an outside party each year.
objectives.evidence: The fence rules per agent, compared with its declaration, and the log of blocked attempts.

objectives.title: Input validation
objectives.statement: Validate every input an agent accepts against what it declares it accepts, so that malformed or hostile input is turned away.
objectives.metric: Share of agents that validate their inputs
tiers: The experiment uses the standard validation library.
Inputs are validated against the declared form.
Validation runs outside the agent's own reasoning, and rejected inputs are logged.
Validation is tested with hostile inputs each quarter.
objectives.evidence: The declared input forms and the validation logs.

objectives.title: Output sanitization
objectives.statement: Clean agent outputs of data that must not leave, such as secrets and data above the recipient's clearance.
tiers: Sandbox output stays in the sandbox.
Outputs are scanned for secrets before they leave.
Outputs are checked against the recipient's clearance, and violations are incidents.
Output checks are tested with seeded data each quarter.
objectives.evidence: Scan logs, incident records and test results.

objectives.title: Current threat models
objectives.statement: Keep a threat model for each agent, and update it when new kinds of attack appear or the agent changes.
objectives.metric: Age of each agent's threat model
tiers: No threat model is required for an experiment.
A standard threat checklist is kept with the agent.
A threat model is reviewed at every change to the agent's reach or authority, and at least each year.
The threat model is reviewed each quarter and shared with internal audit.
objectives.evidence: The threat model with its review dates.

objectives.title: Adversarial testing
objectives.statement: Attack high-tier agents on purpose, through red team exercises, to find weaknesses before others do.
objectives.metric: Share of Tier 3 and higher agents with a red team exercise in the last year
tiers: No exercise is required.
Automated adversarial tests run at release.
A red team exercise runs each year and after major changes.
An outside red team tests the agent each year, and findings are tracked to closure.
objectives.evidence: The exercise reports and the tracking of their findings.

objectives.title: Supply chain integrity
objectives.statement: Verify where every model, component and dependency came from and that it has not been altered, before it is used and while it is in use.
objectives.metric: Share of components with verified provenance
tiers: Components come from approved sources.
Components are pinned, and their sources are recorded in the bill of materials.
Components are verified by signature or checksum at build and at deploy.
Provenance is verified by an outside party each year, including the model suppliers' own attestations.
objectives.evidence: The bill of materials with verification results, and supplier attestations.

objectives.title: Supplier security assessment
objectives.statement: Assess the security of every supplier of agent components or services, and keep the assessments current.
objectives.metric: Share of suppliers with a current assessment
tiers: Experiments use suppliers already approved.
Each supplier has a security questionnaire on file.
Each supplier is assessed each year, with evidence such as an independent audit report.
Critical suppliers are assessed in depth, and the contract gives the right to audit.
objectives.evidence: The supplier assessments and the audit reports they rely on.

objectives.title: Concentration risk
objectives.statement: Watch for dependence on a single supplier of models, infrastructure or services, and keep a plan for replacing it.
tiers: No requirement applies to an experiment.
The agent's single-supplier dependencies are recorded.
Each critical single-supplier dependency has a written exit plan.
Exit plans are tested, and concentration is reported to the governance council.
objectives.evidence: The dependency record, exit plans and test results.

objectives.title: Incident response
objectives.statement: Keep tested response plans for agent security incidents. Record what happened without guessing, and leave the decisions to a person.
objectives.risk: Slow or poor response to an incident
tiers: The sandbox can be shut down on any incident.
Each agent is covered by the organization's incident plan.
Agent-specific playbooks exist and are drilled each year.
Drills include partners and regulators' notice requirements, and run each half year.
objectives.evidence: The playbooks, drill reports and incident records.

objectives.title: Pause and stop
objectives.statement: Let a named person pause or end any agent at once. A stop revokes its credentials, every door checks for the stop so the agent stays stopped, and a paused agent resumes only when that person says so.
objectives.risk: An agent that cannot be stopped
objectives.metric: Share of agents with a stop tested in the last quarter
tiers: The sandbox can be shut down as a whole.
Each agent has a named person who can stop it, and the stop is tested at release.
A stop revokes credentials at once and is checked at every point the agent passes through, and it is tested each quarter.
The stop is tested each month, and its reach across delegated work is measured as the Network discipline requires.
objectives.evidence: The named stoppers, the stop test results and the time each test took to take effect.

objectives.title: Forensic logging
objectives.statement: Log enough, in records nobody can alter unnoticed, to investigate and attribute any security incident involving an agent.
tiers: Sandbox logs are kept for the experiment's life.
Security events are logged centrally.
Logs cannot be changed by the agent or its operators, and are kept for the retention period.
Logs can be handed to an outside investigator without the team's help.
objectives.evidence: The logging settings, a completeness sample and the storage settings that prevent edits.

objectives.title: Each agent's own secrets
objectives.statement: Give every agent its own credentials, never shared with another agent or a person, named in its configuration rather than written into it.
objectives.risk: One leaked secret opening many agents
tiers: Sandbox credentials work only in the sandbox.
Each agent has its own credentials held in a secrets store.
Credentials are short-lived and rotated, and a scan for shared or embedded secrets runs at every build.
Credential use is monitored, and use from an unexpected place stops the agent.
objectives.evidence: The secrets store inventory per agent and the scan results.
